clue.text: Mole's downfall, this itinerant minstrel?

parts.note: a mole is a harbour breakwater, in other words a pier
rot is decay or collapse, as in 'the rot set in'

explanation.surface: A garden mole's undoing is somehow tied to a wandering singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mole' suggests the burrowing animal, but here it is a stone pier, and its downfall is its rot.
explanation.definitionFit: The white-faced clown of French pantomime became the stock figure of travelling seaside entertainers.

clue.text: Psychological remedy for village lad suffering amputation

parts.note: a village is a place

indicators.note: suffering amputation means the word loses its last letter, cut off

parts.note: a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: A treatment for the mind is sought for a country boy who lost a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering amputation' cuts the end off BOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill works only through the patient's belief in it.

clue.text: Cover that's erected on the German upland?

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means the abbreviation is turned upward, reversed

parts.note: i.e. stands for 'that is'
der is German for the
downs are rolling chalk uplands in southern England

explanation.surface: A covering put up on a German hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'erected' reverses IE. Downs are areas of rolling chalk hills in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt filled with duck feathers serves as a bed covering.

clue.text: Elegant introductions to rodents in the zoologists' yearbook

indicators.note: introductions to means the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Stylish openings to the rodents section of a zoological annual.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from the luxurious hotels of César Ritz, so it means flashy or smart.

clue.text: Conservative fellow said to lead state, perhaps

indicators.note: to lead means this piece comes in front
said means the name is heard, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: Terry is a man's name, a fellow
Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative chap is reported to be heading the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' marks a homophone of the man's name; 'to lead' means that sound comes first. 'State, perhaps' hints that a territory is like a state but not quite one.
explanation.definitionFit: A region such as an Australian or Canadian one is an example of a state-like area.

clue.text: Clumsy workman's antipodean mate, about fifty

indicators.note: about means the friend's word goes around the Roman numeral

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a friend
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An Australian's pal, a ham-fisted labourer, is around fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: COBBER is Australian slang for a mate; 'about' puts L (fifty) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cobble is to mend roughly, so a cobbler can mean any bungler.

clue.text: Managed to be dressed in a cloak

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in getting into a cape.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting by means handling things; a cope is a long ecclesiastical cloak, so one wearing it is cloaked.

clue.text: Woman carrying fork threw it in a barn

indicators.note: threw means the letters are tossed about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman with a pitchfork tossed it into a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'fork' is a trident, which the symbolic figure of Britain holds on old coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The female personification of Britain is shown holding a trident.

clue.text: Walk up with a woolly beast

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a mall is a shaded walk, as in The Mall in London

explanation.surface: A woolly creature climbs the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses MALL, a walk, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American pack animal has a thick coat of wool.

clue.text: Leftist's family being brave

parts.note: a red is a leftist or communist
kin are family

explanation.surface: A socialist's relatives prove courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective but is the noun for a Native American warrior; the answer is a dated and offensive term.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave was a North American Indian warrior, for which this old word is now offensive.

clue.text: University's external entrance examination by accountants

indicators.note: external says the mine entrance sits on the outside, around the university's letter

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A college's outside gate is being inspected by the bean-counters.
explanation.walkthrough: ADIT, a mine entrance, is 'external' to U for university.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of a firm's books is carried out by accountants.

clue.text: Salesman has edge — and supplies rocket

parts.note: rep is short for a sales representative
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A salesman has an edge and supplies a firework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocket' is British slang for a severe telling-off, not a firework.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting a rocket in British speech means receiving a stern rebuke.

clue.text: Archaeopteryx, perhaps — not one to go hungry

explanation.surface: A prehistoric feathered creature is described as never going without food.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaeopteryx was one of the first feathered creatures in history; the proverb says the first riser catches the worm, so never starves.

clue.text: Coarse linen Finn left behind

indicators.note: left means the Finn's word is departed, removed from the fabric's name

parts.note: huckaback is a coarse linen towelling
Huck Finn is Mark Twain's boy hero, so Finn gives HUCK

explanation.surface: A rough cloth from Finland has been abandoned somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finn' looks like a man from Finland; it is Huckleberry Finn, giving HUCK, which leaves the end of HUCKABACK.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means backwards or to the rear, as in a ship's sails laid back.

clue.text: In a classical poet there's nothing like Humpty Dumpty

indicators.note: In says the zero is placed inside the poet's name

parts.note: Ovid was the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Inside an old Roman poet there's nothing resembling a nursery-rhyme figure.
explanation.walkthrough: O for nothing goes inside OVID.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme character is drawn as an egg, so he is egg-shaped.

clue.text: It's a waste of time raising a complaint during a ball

indicators.note: during places the turned piece in the middle of the ball word

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the words are lifted, read upward

parts.note: an ill is an ailment

explanation.surface: Complaining at a ball is said to be pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns 'a complaint' upward to LLIA, and 'during' sets it inside the ball; 'a waste of time' is a fair noun phrase for idle trifling.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle flirting or trifling is time frittered away.

clue.text: Port? No, gin — distributed in Kentish Town

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are spread about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker refuses port and wants gin, served around a town in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges PORT NO GIN. Orpington is a town in Kent, south-east England, also famous for its chicken breed.
explanation.definitionFit: This suburban town lies in the county of Kent, in south-east England.

clue.text: Some raised land associated with a fruit tree?

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for the bird linked with one

parts.note: part means some of something
a ridge is raised land

explanation.surface: A stretch of high ground is connected with an orchard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the carol 'The Twelve Days of Christmas' with its bird in a pear tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Christmas carol, the game bird famously sits in a pear tree.

clue.text: Attendant upholds right to identify publication here

indicators.note: upholds in a down clue means one piece sits above, holding up the other

parts.note: title means a right or claim, as in title to land
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: A servant supports someone's claim to name a book.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upholds' puts the attendant beneath TITLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf at the front of a book gives its name and publisher details.

clue.text: Pit 15, possibly, used to plant explosive devices

parts.note: a mine is a pit dug for coal
an Orpington is a breed of hen, which is a layer of eggs

explanation.surface: A coal pit in Orpington is put to use planting bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: '15' refers to the answer at 15 across, a hen breed, so 'possibly' makes it an example of a LAYER.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship of this kind is built to lay mines at sea.

clue.text: 'Then, in a friend, it is cold _____' (J Caesar)

definitions.text: 'Then, in a friend, it is cold _____' (J Caesar)

parts.words: 'Then, in a friend, it is cold _____' (J Caesar)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Antony's speech over Caesar's body in Shakespeare's play

explanation.walkthrough: Mark Antony, shaking the conspirators' hands, says that to stay silent would be cold restraint in a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line names the quality of humble reticence that Antony says would be cold in a friend.

clue.text: Shortly William Hill will take the stage

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the performer who does so

parts.note: William shortly is Bill, and a bill is an account, abbreviated A/C
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's shop will soon be appearing in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'William Hill' looks like the British bookmaker; split it. Bill (short for William) is an account, A/C, and a tor is a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer is one whose job is to go on stage in plays.

clue.text: Rex, trendy fellow, seen gaping

parts.note: R stands for Rex, king
in means fashionable
a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A trendy chap called Rex is seen with his mouth open.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a rare botanical word for two-lipped flowers that gape open.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical term describes something wide open, like a gaping mouth.

clue.text: Garment stolen in the centre of Sardinia

indicators.note: in places the stolen word inside the middle letters
the centre of means the middle two letters of the island's name

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing was nicked in the heart of a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the centre of' takes the two middle letters of an eight-letter island name; 'in' puts the slang for stolen goods there. A dhoti is the loincloth worn by Hindu men.
explanation.definitionFit: A loincloth worn by Hindu men in India is a piece of clothing.

clue.text: Frequently concerning the heartless knight

parts.note: of can mean concerning, as in 'speak of'

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Often a story about a cruel knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes H from THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Many times or repeatedly.

clue.text: West Indian takes a 24 arranged in prison

indicators.note: in puts the inner letters within the prison word

parts.note: the can is slang for prison

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the answer at 24 are reordered

parts.note: the answer at 24 down, an inducement

explanation.surface: A man from the islands accepts a sweetener set up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles the answer at 24 down into RIBBE; 'in' puts A plus that inside the slang word for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers the islands and people of the sea between the Americas.

clue.text: Food licked with relish?

explanation.surface: Something to eat is savoured with a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuts of lamb or pork are meat; people lick their jaws when they relish something.

clue.text: Inducement to live without a woman

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside places the verb around the woman

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
rib is jocular slang for a woman, from Eve made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: A temptation to live alone without a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here has its old sense of outside, so the verb wraps the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment offered to persuade someone dishonestly is an incentive.

clue.text: Cabinet-maker rested among the trees

parts.note: sat means rested on a seat
in means among
a wood is a stand of trees

explanation.surface: A furniture craftsman took a break in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet-maker' is not a person but the timber cabinets are made from.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy yellowish hardwood prized for fine furniture makes good cabinets.

clue.text: One charge that makes us mad!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A single fee is enough to make customers furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad in the sense of angry or furious.

clue.text: Statesmen returned to look for a negative vote

indicators.note: returned means the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: to seek is to look for
nay is a vote against

explanation.surface: Politicians came back to seek a vote against.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses SEEK + NAY. 'Statesmen' is read as men of the States, Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans are men from the United States, a pun on politicians.

clue.text: Climbing it is most demanding without the leader

indicators.note: without the leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: severest means hardest, most demanding

explanation.surface: Climbing a mountain is hardest when your guide is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a comment on the world's highest mountain; SEVEREST loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan peak is the world's highest and the climb most coveted.
